summary: Stop run-owned schedules during cleanup and fence terminal schedule owners

replay.detail: No projection or replay changes. Stops and diagnostics use existing claim kinds.

schema.detail: No storage or wire schema changes. Cancellation and reconciliation diagnostics add schedule-owner-run-terminal and schedule-owner-step-terminal codes.

rules.detail: Cleanup stops owned intake by exact subject identity before waiting on unresolved effects. Schedule arming, timer dispatch and queued-work admission reject terminal run or step owners independently of cleanup. A reconciliation pass durably stops leftover schedules whose owners are already terminal.

compatibility.detail: Run-owned schedules no longer outlive terminal runs; step-owned schedules no longer outlive completed, failed, cancelled or skipped steps. Existing leftovers are affected without a migration. Schedules intended to survive their creator must be declared independently without run or step ownership. Unowned schedules and already-started scheduled mission runs are unchanged.

downtime.detail: No data migration or downtime is required; the lifetime fence takes effect when the updated daemon runs.

manual.detail: Review schedules intentionally created inside short-lived steps or runs. Declare long-lived schedules independently rather than relying on a terminal owner. During a mixed-version rollout, older daemons do not enforce the new dispatch fence.

recovery.detail: Durable stop declarations survive daemon restart and binary rollback. To restore an intentionally long-lived schedule, explicitly redeclare it independently; rolling back alone does not undo stops.
